result:
I've finished the read-only pass. Nothing was built, run or edited, and I skipped `web/.next/`, so Q3 is reasoned from config and code rather than from build output.

## 1. What can go and what must stay

**Browser UI only (safe to delete):**
- `web/app/page.tsx`, `web/app/layout.tsx`, `web/app/globals.css` and `web/app/icon.svg`.
- All of `web/components/*` (19 files). Only `page.tsx` imports them. No route in `web/app/api`, `web/app/eve` or `web/lib` imports `components/` or `public/` (grep came back empty).
- `web/lib/use-shell.ts` and `web/lib/use-agent-thread.ts`, both `"use client"` hooks with no other importers.
- `web/postcss.config.mjs`. It only loads Tailwind, and `globals.css:1` is `@import "tailwindcss"`.
- `web/public/*`: favicons, `site.webmanifest`, `apple-touch-icon` and `brand/*`. These are browser assets. The Swift apps read `brand/` at the repo root (`macos/build-app.sh:63-72`), not `web/public`.

**Must stay:**
- All of `web/app/api/**` and `web/app/eve/v1/[...path]/route.ts`. `BackendClient.swift` calls every one of them except the three below:
  - `/api/health`, `/api/status`, `/api/shell`, `/api/agent/{state,tick,widget,media,image}`, `/api/auth/session`, `/api/approvals`, `/api/attachments`
  - `/api/connections/widget`, `/api/connectors`, `/api/connectors/own-app`, `/api/memory`, `/api/providers[/oauth]`, `/api/routines`, `/api/usage`, `/api/workspace`, `eve/v1/session/*`
- Also keep the three routes with no in-tree client:
  - `/api/connections/callback` and `/api/connectors/callback` are OAuth redirect targets hit by the external browser, so keep them.
  - `/api/reviewer` has no caller under `macos/Sources`, `ios`, `agent`, `shared` or the UI. It looks dead, but I didn't chase it.
  - `/api/connections/widget/[id]/call` is a child of the widget route, so keep it with that route.
- All of `web/lib` except the two hooks. `agent-exec`, `api-guard`, `auth`, `desktop-gate`, `ingress`, `cookie-sessions`, `runtime-config`, `sync-models`, `image-regenerate`, `media-migrate` and `connectors-callback` are used by routes. Tests import `agent-exec`, `api-guard`, `ingress`, `auth`, `sync-models`, `media-migrate` and `image-regenerate` from `test/*.test.ts`.
- `web/next.config.ts`, `web/tsconfig.json` and `web/next-env.d.ts`. `build-app.sh:40` does `git checkout -- web/next-env.d.ts`.
- `shared/chat-markdown.ts` stays. `test/chat-markdown.test.ts` imports it from `shared/`, not from `web/`.

## 2. What breaks or needs changing

- **`macos/build-app.sh:32-33`** runs `cp -R web/public …` under `set -eu`. If `web/public` is gone, the build aborts before `swift build`. Line 32 also copies `web/.next/static`. An API-only build may still emit that folder, but I couldn't confirm it without building.
- **`scripts/web-mode.mjs:74`** requires `web/.next/standalone/web/public` and `…/.next/static` to exist.
  - In a checkout, a missing folder means `webLaunch` silently returns `{mode:"dev", reason:"web_build_missing"}` (line 84). The service then runs `next dev` (`service.mjs:255-263`) and the app looks fine.
  - In a release runtime (line 78-81) it throws `"release runtime has no complete web build"`.
  - Fix: drop `public` (and `static`, if the build no longer emits it) from `copied`.
- **`test/web-mode.test.ts`** lines 22 and 58 fixture and assert the `public` folder. Update them together with the change above. Line 16 (`web/app/page.tsx`) is only a fixture file and is harmless.
- **`scripts/build-brand-assets.mjs`** writes `web/app/icon.svg` (line 208), `web/public/${name}` (238) and `web/public/brand/**` (358, 360). It fails or recreates the deleted files.
- **`scripts/check-brand-assets.mjs`** requires `web/public` (lines 30, 144, 208). `npm run brand:check` fails once the folder is gone. Both brand scripts need the `web/` targets removed.
- **`scripts/web-mode.mjs:10,14`** lists `web/components`, `web/public` and `web/postcss.config.mjs` as sources. Missing paths are tolerated (`throwIfNoEntry:false`, line 26), so nothing crashes. But any deletion changes the source hash.
  - The installed app then serves `next dev` until the next `build:app`, per CLAUDE.md. That is expected, not a fault.
- **`scripts/verify-release.mjs`**:
  - `tsc_web` (line 78) should still pass, since `web/tsconfig.json` globs `**/*.tsx` and matching nothing is fine.
  - `next_build` (line 87) should still pass. Confirm that a Next app directory with only route handlers and no `layout.tsx` builds on 16.2.1. I believe it does, but it needs a real build.
  - Deleting `layout.tsx` removes the `next/font/google` Geist Mono fetch, which today needs network at build time.
- **`macos/Sources/**`** only mentions the deleted files in doc comments (ChatView, RailView, DesignTokens, etc.). Nothing breaks, but the comments go stale.
- **`ios/UsefulBot/Platform/NativeTheme.swift:5`** is a comment pointing at `web/app/globals.css`.
- **Docs**: `HANDOFF.md:59,75,120` are now stale.
- **`perf/`, `ops/`, `services/`, `router/src`, `agent/` and `shared/`** have no references to the UI files.
- **Not affected**: `package.json` scripts (`web:dev`, `web:build`) and `next.config.ts`, since routes still need Next.

## 3. Would a packaged release still start its web service?

**Today, most likely yes.** `build-runtime.mjs` copies `web/.next/standalone` whole (lines 52 and 80), so it needs no `web/` sources.
- The server sits at `<runtime>/web/.next/standalone/web/server.js`, and `outputFileTracingRoot` is the repo root (`next.config.ts:16`).
- `require("next")` walks up from that folder through `standalone/web/node_modules`, then `standalone/node_modules`, and Next's traced copy is found there.
- The trimmed root `node_modules/next` and `@next` (build-runtime lines 106-112) are further up the walk, so that deletion doesn't matter.
- Anything nft could not trace, such as a native package or a dynamic require, falls back to the root `node_modules` from `npm ci --omit=dev`.
- I could not confirm the traced `standalone/node_modules` contents without inspecting `.next`, so today's answer is probable, not proven.

**After the change, yes, if three things hold:**
- `next`, `react` and `react-dom` stay in `dependencies`.
- The `public` and `static` checks are fixed as in section 2.
- The API-only build still emits `server.js` under `standalone/web/`.

Only the tracing input changes, so resolution should behave the same. A release that keeps the `public` check but has no `public` folder fails at `web-mode.mjs:79-81`. Test this by running `UB_RELEASE=1 build:app`, then starting from the staged runtime.

## 4. Dependencies that become unused

- `tailwindcss` 4.3.3 and `@tailwindcss/postcss` 4.3.3 are used only by `postcss.config.mjs` and `globals.css`. Remove both.
- `react`, `react-dom`, `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` have no non-UI consumer. Keep `react` and `react-dom`, though. `next` lists them as peers (`package-lock.json` marks them `peer: true`), and I don't know that an API-only `next build` works without them. Keep the two `@types` packages too, since Next's TypeScript setup check tends to install them. This is inferred, so removing them is a test, not a certainty.
- `next` stays, because it serves the API routes.

**What else must change if you remove the Tailwind pair:**
- **The lockfile hash.** `package-lock.json` changes, and the router refuses to start (`router/src/registry.ts:80-90`, `503 configuration_unverified`) unless `packageLockHash` in `shared/registry.json:23,46` is updated to the new hash. Tests that read `registry.json` will need the same update.
- **`build-runtime.mjs:93-105`** requires that `npm ci` leave the lockfile byte-identical. Regenerate the lock with `npm install --package-lock-only`, not through a Next build. `build-app.sh:14-18` warns that Next's TypeScript auto-install rewrites the lockfile.
- **`package.json` is a source in the hash** (`web-mode.mjs:14`), so the installed app runs `next dev` until the next `build:app`.

## Findings

1. Nothing under `web/app/api` or `web/app/eve` is UI-only, so keep every route. Delete only `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `globals.css`, `icon.svg`, all of `web/components/`, the two `use-*.ts` hooks, `postcss.config.mjs` and `web/public/`.
2. `macos/build-app.sh:32` (`cp -R web/public`) aborts the build under `set -eu`, and `web/.next/static` (line 31) is unverified for an API-only build. Remove or guard both copies.
3. `scripts/web-mode.mjs:74` still requires `public` and `static`. A checkout silently falls back to `next dev`, and a release throws `release runtime has no complete web build`. Trim `copied` and update `test/web-mode.test.ts:22,58`.
4. `build-brand-assets.mjs` (208, 238, 358, 360) and `check-brand-assets.mjs` (30, 144, 208) still target `web/public` and `web/app/icon.svg`. Drop the web targets.
5. Removing Tailwind changes `package-lock.json`, which makes the router refuse to start until `shared/registry.json:23,46` carries the new hash. Regenerate the lock with `--package-lock-only`, then update the hash and its tests in the same change.
6. Keep `next`, `react` and `react-dom` (plus the two `@types` packages) unless a real API-only build and release stage prove otherwise. Remove only `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/postcss`.
7. Release start-up depends on tracing, not on the deletions. `server.js` finds `next` in `standalone/node_modules` before the root one that `build-runtime.mjs:108` trims. Prove it by running `UB_RELEASE=1 build:app` and starting the staged runtime.
8. Unverified: a `layout`-less, route-only app directory building on Next 16.2.1, and `.next/static` being emitted. Both are checkable with one `next build`.
9. `verify-release.mjs` needs no change. Update the stale comments in the Swift files and `HANDOFF.md` and the `NativeTheme.swift` comment. `/api/reviewer` has no visible caller and is worth a separate look.
